prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (2005 manifesto)

- Economics and taxation:
  - Add higher income tax bands (indicative: 50% over £50k; 60% over £100k) and more corporation tax bands (40% on profits over £1.5m).
  - Shift tax from earned income and employment to unearned income and wealth; replace National Insurance with income-based taxation.
  - Pilot a Land Value Tax set locally to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
  - Phase out VAT and introduce revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes tied to resource use, pollution and waste (including aviation fuel; plastic bags).
  - Promote economic localisation via community banks, credit unions, micro‑credit, local currencies; oppose joining the euro.
  - Support workers’ rights, union representation, reduced working hours; job creation via renewable energy, zero‑waste and low‑carbon transport.
  - Replace GDP with broader well‑being measures (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

- Energy and climate:
  - Adopt Contraction and Convergence: cut CO2 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030 (1990 baseline); develop full carbon trading.
  - Replace domestic VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content, with protections for low users.
  - Target 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; support solar, wind (on/offshore), wave and biogas.
  - Warmer Homes Act to cut domestic energy demand 30% in 10 years; “Smart Energy Councils” to deliver 45% emission cuts by 2020.
  - Decommission nuclear stations at end of life; end nuclear R&D subsidies.

- Welfare and housing:
  - Phase in a universal, unconditional Citizen’s Income to replace most means‑tested benefits; retain and later integrate housing benefit; keep disability/incapacity supplements.
  - Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension linked to average earnings, replacing Pension Credit (initially at Pension Credit Guarantee level).
  - Simplify child support; raise child benefit; reduce maximum working hours (end 48‑hour opt‑out; assess 35‑hour average).
  - Expand early years support (Children’s Centres); boost social/affordable housing: allow council reinvestment of receipts, support self‑build co‑ops, improve insulation/efficiency.

- Health and education:
  - Reinforce a comprehensive, universal NHS; end market/PPP approaches; oppose GATS extension into healthcare.
  - Abolish prescription charges; restore free eye tests and NHS dentistry; expand access to complementary treatments.
  - Raise health funding to at least pre‑2004 EU average (~9% of GNP; ~£90bn by 2008); consider a hypothecated NHS tax.
  - Increase education funding (pre‑school and post‑16), scrap tuition fees, restore maintenance grants (later integrated with Citizen’s Income).
  - Abolish SATs at 7/11/14; introduce voluntary Individual Learning Plans.

- Transport:
  - Prioritise walking, cycling, public transport; target 10% road traffic reduction by 2010; re‑regulate buses; invest £30bn shifted from road building.
  - Return rail and tube track/operations to public ownership; expand lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
  - Reflect full motoring costs (congestion/road pricing; higher fuel duty; abolish car tax disc); size/axle/pollution‑based freight duty; back R&D for efficient vehicles.
  - Curb aviation growth: resist new runways, ban night flights, raise APD, EU‑level fuel tax; UK emissions tax on domestic flights.

- Environment and animal welfare:
  - Zero Waste Strategy and agency; Waste Reduction, Re‑use and Recycling Bill; outlaw incineration; recycled‑content standards; 60% domestic recycling by 2010.
  - Create an Environmental Protection Commission; eco‑taxes on aggregates, pesticides, organochlorines, fossil fuels; strengthen EU chemicals rules.
  - Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; oppose patents on natural genetic resources (revise TRIPS).
  - End live animal exports; ban battery eggs (including “enriched”); seek strict EU broiler rules; ban fur imports; replace vivisection with humane methods.

- Food and farming:
  - Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support farmers’ markets, box schemes, co‑ops.
  - Replace CAP/CFP with support for organic/local production, biodiversity, and sustainable incomes; ban GM food.
  - Strengthen and enforce a binding supermarkets’ Code of Practice; independent watchdog; review mergers in convenience retail.

- Crime and justice:
  - Prevention via urban design, youth facilities, rapid repair, staffed public spaces; treat drug use primarily as a health issue; reject national ID cards and redirect costs to prevention.
  - Expand community policing: more officers, local stations, neighbourhood committees; restore roles like park keepers.
  - Tighten gun laws: quantitative lethality threshold; prohibit specified firearms; license deactivated guns; single rigorous licensing with competence and stability tests.
  - Expand restorative justice; strengthen responses to hate crime and violence against women; support a comprehensive disability directive.

- Democracy and constitutional change:
  - Oppose national ID cards; renew empowered local government with Land Value Tax; enable local recalls/referenda.
  - Introduce proportional representation for local councils and Westminster; democratise regional governance; consider further devolution for Scotland/Wales.
  - Fully elected second chamber by PR; draft a written constitution; disestablish the state church; remove formal royal powers.
  - Oppose the proposed EU constitution; seek a more democratic, transparent EU.

- International policy:
  - Pursue diplomacy, conflict prevention, arms control, and nuclear disarmament; withdraw from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers; reduce defence spending to EU average.
  - End subsidies/credits for arms exports; close export‑promotion bodies; seek a binding Arms Trade Treaty; renounce CBW and depleted uranium.
  - Raise overseas aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest countries; promote a Tobin tax; use North‑South carbon trading.
  - Reform UN Security Council (end permanent seats/veto; majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
  - Overhaul/replace WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade enabling localisation and rights/environment standards.
  - On asylum/migration: faster, fairer decisions; right to work and benefits; independent appeals; ratify the UN Migrant Workers Convention; uphold the 1951 Refugee Convention; review domestic legislation on access and support.
